target.title: fix(qqbot): add timeout to remote media URL fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QQBot remote media downloads accepted HTTPS media URLs and delegated them through the platform media adapter without a response-header deadline. If a remote media host accepted the connection but never sent headers, inbound attachment handling or outbound remote-media send preparation could wait indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared media runtime now has a `responseHeaderTimeoutMs` contract for stalled-header protection. This PR wires QQBot's media adapter contract through to that runtime and gives `downloadFile()` a 120s response-header deadline while preserving the existing HTTPS and SSRF policy checks.

This deliberately does not use `timeoutMs` for the QQBot 120s deadline, because `timeoutMs` caps the complete fetch/body operation and can break slow-but-progressing media downloads after headers arrive.

## User Impact

QQBot media URLs that stall before response headers now fail and return `null` through the existing error path instead of wedging the media pipeline forever. Slow response bodies can continue through the existing media runtime body handling after headers arrive.

## Evidence

Exact head: `2a5ab12210ce48a1925620a7bcc621de2daa7716`

Current-head validation:

- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts` -> 2 files, 7 tests passed.
- Format: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/qqbot/src/engine/adapter/types.ts extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.ts extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts` -> passed.
- Lint: `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 extensions/qqbot/src/engine/adapter/types.ts extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.ts extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts` -> passed.
- Whitespace: `git diff --check` -> clean.
- Types: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental false --pretty false` -> passed.
- Autoreview: `env -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u OPENAI_ORG_ID -u OPENAI_PROJECT_ID .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` -> passed with no findings.

Current-head behavior coverage:

- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts` asserts `downloadFile()` passes `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000` together with `QQBOT_MEDIA_SSRF_POLICY` to the platform adapter.
- `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts` asserts the built-in bridge adapter forwards `responseHeaderTimeoutMs` through to `readRemoteMediaBuffer()`.
- `src/media/fetch.ts` on current `main` owns the response-header timer and clears only that timer after headers arrive; this PR does not add a duplicate core media path.

Previously accepted real behavior proof:

- At previous exact head `fb6cf168380c2894040fc279aa1bfa203b8e95e7`, the local stalled HTTPS harness exercised production `downloadFile()` from `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.ts`, the built-in adapter from `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.ts`, the media runtime, the SSRF guard, a real HTTPS/TLS connection, and the production 120000ms abort path.
- That harness used `https://media.qq.com:<port>/redacted/photo.png`, mapped `media.qq.com` to `198.18.0.1`, enabled the QQBot RFC2544 SSRF allowance, withheld response headers, observed the client abort after the 120s deadline, returned `downloadFile.result=null`, and wrote zero files.
- Current-head rerun of that exact local network harness was blocked by the container network permissions: `ip addr add 198.18.0.1/32 dev lo` returned `RTNETLINK answers: Operation not permitted`. The current-head focused tests above cover the code difference from that accepted proof: the 120s deadline now lands in `responseHeaderTimeoutMs` instead of `timeoutMs`.

What was not tested: live QQBot traffic. No QQBot token, media ID, or secret was used.
